stem:
The diagram shows kite $ABCD$ that Bharti draws. Equal marks show $AB=BC$ and $AD=DC$. Diagonal $BD$ is drawn solid; diagonal $AC$ is dashed.

Which claim about the kite and its special diagonal is correct?

options.text: The kite has all four sides equal because the diagram shows four sides.
Diagonal $AC$ is the axis of symmetry of the kite.
Diagonal $BD$ is the axis of symmetry; it bisects $AC$ at right angles.
The figure is a kite because it is labelled $ABCD$.

teacher.key_rationale: With AB=BC and AD=DC, BD is the symmetry diagonal: it bisects AC at right angles. Claiming all sides equal, swapping to AC, or relying on the label alone miss that property.
teacher.figure_note: Kite ABCD with equal marks on AB=BC and AD=DC; BD solid, AC dashed.
